newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ERM decision not vital to monetary policy-Riksbank.
newsitem.headline: ERM decision not vital to monetary policy-Riksbank.

text.p: A future Swedish decision on whether to join Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) has no crucial implications for monetary policy, central bank governor Urban Backstrom said in a newspaper interview on Friday.
"The decision has no crucial implications for monetary policy," Backstrom told daily Dagens Nyheter.
"It'll be fine to arrange our figures with the combination we have now of a fixed inflation goal and a moveable exchange rate.
"However the link to ERM is present in a high degree in the question of Sweden's relations with other European countries."
Backstrom said the central bank, the Riksbank, was ready to link the crown to the ERM but there was no active preparations for it.
He said that only one political party, the Moderates, is recommending the link.

"In the present situation there is a risk that linking the crown to ERM would awaken active political opposition. This would not create confidence and on the contrary would be counterproductive for an ERM link," Backstrom said.
Backstrom said he saw an ERM link mainly as a way to increase Sweden's chance of joining the EU's Economic and Monetary Union that comes into effect on January 1, 1999.
But the link itself still had to be discussed.

"The main scenario is that it is important to have a stable currency for at least two years irrespective of going into ERM or not. But many give a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty's demand for ERM-links," Backstrom said.

A big advantage of linking to the ERM would be that Sweden would not in future have to defend the crown actively, as was the case in 1992. "A link to ERM would indicate that Sweden will hold onto low inflation and healthy public finances," he said.

Backstrom said that in the present situation, wage increases do not threaten to boost inflation. But he warned that price rises would threaten inflation if there were wage increases as big as during 1996.
"I hope that we never need to see (interest) rates as high as over the past few years. But for this inflation must remain low and people need to risk a little for that," Backstrom said.
